All users — specifically screen reader users who rely on breadcrumbs for orientation, keyboard-only users navigating via Tab, low vision users using screen magnifiers to follow the breadcrumb trail. 4. Each item except the last is a link to its corresponding parent page; the last item (current page) is static text with no link behavior. The component must support variable depth (2-5 levels) and clearly indicate which breadcrumb represents the user's current location. **User needs:** - Screen reader users need orientation within site hierarchy — breadcrumbs provide essential context about their location relative to parent categories - Keyboard-only users need efficient navigation through the breadcrumb trail using Tab key - Low vision users benefit from clear visual distinction between navigable links and non-navigable current page indicator **Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 AA (all success criteria cited throughout this document) **Assistive technologies supported:** NVDA (Windows), VoiceOver (macOS/iOS), keyboard-only navigation **Risk factors:** - Variable depth (2-5 levels) requires consistent behavior across all depths - Incorrect separator handling can create confusing screen reader announcements ("Home, greater than sign, Products") - Missing aria-current="page" leaves screen reader users without knowledge of their current location - Making current page focusable or a link confuses navigation expectations **Constraints:** CSS-only separators (hidden from screen readers), variable depth support (2-5 levels), clear current page indicator needed. --- ## Semantic Structure Plan The breadcrumb uses the APG Breadcrumb pattern: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumbs/ ### Structure Diagram ```html

The nav element itself is not focusable, but its child anchors are in natural tab order following DOM sequence. Current page item (static text) is NOT focusable and does not participate in tab order. Example tab sequence for "Home > Products > Electronics > Laptops": - Tab 1: Home link - Tab 2: Products link - Tab 3: Electronics link - (Laptops — current page, static text, NOT focusable) - Next Tab: moves to next interactive element on the page ### Focus Traps None needed. Breadcrumbs are a simple linear navigation sequence with no modal or overlay behavior requiring focus containment per WCAG 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap. ### Focus Restoration Not applicable. No overlays or modals involved in breadcrumb interaction — there's nothing to restore focus from when closing. ### Dynamic Content Insertion Focus Management When breadcrumbs update dynamically (e.g., user navigates to a new category via SPA routing), the nav landmark updates but focus should NOT automatically move. This would interrupt users who are interacting with other page elements. The aria-current="page" attribute on the new current item will be announced if the screen reader re-reads the region, but automatic focus movement is not appropriate here per WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (focus order should follow meaningful sequence, not jump unexpectedly). ### Focus Indicators - Native browser default focus outline is sufficient for breadcrumb links — it provides a visible rectangle around focused anchors with adequate contrast against adjacent colors - If custom focus styling is applied, must meet WCAG 2.4.7: 3:1 contrast ratio between focused and unfocused states, minimum 2px perimeter area (WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance) - Focus indicator should be clearly visible at all zoom levels up to 200% per WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow ### Skip Link Consideration The nav with aria-label="Breadcrumb" serves as a landmark that screen reader users can navigate to directly via rotor/landmark navigation. A separate skip link is not needed for breadcrumbs themselves, but the page should have a standard "Skip to main content" link at the top per WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks. ### Roving Tabindex Not applicable — breadcrumb links are simple anchors in natural tab order with no composite widget behavior requiring roving tabindex management. --- ## State Communication Design ### States Table | State | Visual Indicator | Programmatic Indicator | ARIA Attribute | WCAG Citation | |-------|-----------------|----------------------|-----------------|---------------| | Current page (Laptops) | Static text, no underline, no hover effect, visually distinct from links (e.g., default text color vs link blue) | `aria-current="page"` on the `

Separator color should have sufficient contrast to be visible but doesn't need to meet the full 4.5:1 since it's decorative (WCAG 1.4.3 applies to meaningful text, not purely decorative elements) ### Non-Color Alternatives for All Color-Coded Information - Links are distinguished from current page by more than just color — links have underlines and pointer cursors; current page is plain static text without underline or hover effect per WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color - If link color alone were used to distinguish navigable items, it would fail WCAG 1.4.1 — the combination of underline + color ensures non-color alternative ### Font Sizing Strategy - Use relative units (rem/em) for breadcrumb text size per WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text - Base font size typically inherited from page body (usually 16px = 1rem) - Breadcrumb text should resize proportionally with user's browser zoom settings up to 200% without horizontal scroll per WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow ### Responsive Text and Line Spacing - Line height at least 1.5 × font size per WCAG 1.4.8 Visual Presentation - Letter spacing adequate for readability (at least 0.12 × font size) - Paragraph spacing adequate if breadcrumbs wrap to multiple lines ### Animation and Motion - No animations or transitions in breadcrumb component — no prefers-reduced-motion consideration needed - If CSS hover effects include transitions, they should respect `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` media query per WCAG 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions ### Dark Mode / Color Scheme Preference - Colors must meet contrast ratios in both light and dark modes if supporting `prefers-color-scheme: dark` per WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast - Link colors, current page text, and separator colors all need verification in both themes ### Touch Target Sizing - Breadcrumb links should be at least 24x24 CSS pixels (WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size Minimum), ideally 44x44 recommended - Ensure adequate padding around link text to meet minimum touch target size, especially on mobile devices where breadcrumb links may be short words like "Home" ### Content Reflow at 400% Zoom -
